Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers, which is why the background data used from Swedish sawmills can be considered representative of this consumption.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When the products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective.
Resources.GeneralComment: Input are collected from 44 sawmills and cover the production of 10 190 000 m³ sawn dried timber. Data to produce sawn wood is collected from a representative selection of sawmills in Sweden and weighted to an average. Sawn dried timber that is produced in Sweden is mainly based on domestic logs. The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for sawn timbers varies between 21-37 kg CO₂e/m³ for the companies that are involved (and based on the methodology and inventory data used).
Resources.Name: Sawn timber, u 16 %, coniferous
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of wood indoors is normally equal to the construction of which it is part of. Wood exposed to outdoors normally needs maintenance during these 50 years lifespan.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Sawn timber can be used directly as it is and serves as a raw material for impregnated wood. When it is planed, it is used for other wood-based products. Sawn timber is used in construction for formwork and structural timber, for so-called cladding timber for panels, as well as planed for flooring or joinery timber for windows, doors, and interior fittings, etc. The wood is usually refined by planing, profiling, gluing, finger-jointing, or impregnation depending on the area of use.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The climate impact is based on a sector EPD that cover 58 % of the total sawn softwood timber in Sweden. Dried sawn timber has an average density of 455 kg/m³ and moisture content of 16 %. Sawn dried timber of spruce has an average density of 470 kg/m³ and 440 kg/m³ for pine. The moisture content for the dried wood is about 12-18 %. Biogenic carbon storage is 715kg CO₂/m³.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the major producers and thereby the major consumption of sawn timber used in Sweden. These data represent the year 2020, i.e. after reduction diesel was implemented why the GWP reported is lower than before.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative of sawn dried timber and can be used as it is, but is mainly used as a raw material in planed wood production.

Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producer, but significantly import occurs from (given in relative order); Norway, Finland and Europe.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: The specific board is designed to be used indoors and has a common thickness of 12.5 mm.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for gypsum board typically varies between different manufacturers within +/- 0.3 kg CO₂e/kg. The average data values are based on the EPDs and market share of sold products. The products are manufactured in the following countries (in the order of market share): Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland.
Resources.Name: Gypsum, standard plasterboard
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part of.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: The product is particularly suitable for the cladding of internal walls, ceilings and partitions in all types of buildings. This type of plasterboard is usually used as a surface material in a moisture-protected indoor environment.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Plasterboards are based on a mixture of virgin gypsum, waste gypsum, and recycled gypsum. Densities between different producers varies +/-2 %. Paperboard surfacing has a typical value of 360 g/m².
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative for a standard gypsum board used for general purpose indoors.

Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Concrete manufacturers are spread across the entire country, and the environmental data can be considered representative since the concrete recipes used, as well as the binder mix, reflect the production of all these manufacturers and are also based on several EPDs.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When concrete products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, i.e. the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.GeneralComment: Concrete is made from rock, gravel and cement where the main raw material is limestone. In climate-improved concrete is part of the cement replaced with alternative binders. The data given, based on compressive strength class, represent commonly used concrete recipes on the market. Factory data for module A3 is based on data from a large number of EPDs. Of the reported value for climate impact, the contribution from the manufacturing process (A3) is relatively small in relation to the contribution from the cement, which normally accounts for more than 90 % of the concrete's climate impact in module A1-A3. Environmental data for the cement binders used are based on EPDs for commonly used cement grades on the Swedish market.
Resources.Name: Ready-mix made concrete, buildings C25/30
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: Concrete exposed to outdoors or other wet environment is designed in respect to durability according to Eurocodes. The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of. Concrete for buildings usually does not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Concrete for houses is used especially for load-bearing parts of the structure. The concrete composition is controlled, in addition to compressive strength of exposure class, but also of other properties e.g. consistence, time for curing and drying.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The compressive strength class of the concrete follows the standard EN 206:2013+A1:2016 and SS 137003:2015.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The provided data are representative of the Swedish producers of ready-mixed concrete and the concrete recipes they use. This information was collected in 2020. The environmental impact data are based on current EPDs for binders as well as factory data.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet:
The compressive strength classes refer to concrete used for buildings with a concrete composition and binder mix representative of the Swedish market. If more properties are required for a concrete, information from a supplier must be used. Normally, concrete is reinforced. Reinforcement is handled as a separate resource in this database.
For testing compressive strength, EN 206 refers to the following standard: EN 12390-3, Testing hardened concrete — Part 3: Compressive strength of test specimens. In Table 12 of EN 206 specifies "Compressive strength classes for normal concrete and heavy concrete". This is supplemented in SS 137003 with "Table 1 — Intermediate classes for compressive strength".

Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: All bricks used in Sweden are imported (the last brickyard was located at Haga, Enköping and was closed in 2020. A very small production based on old technology is nowadays left at Horns Tegelbruk). The largest imports come from Denmark and then from Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When bricks are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.GeneralComment: Bricks are manufactured of clay, sand, lime and sawdust. The bricks are burned in a tunnel furnace at a high temperature, roughly 1050 degrees. The primary energy use varies between 2.0 – 4 MJ/kg of nonrenewable energy and 0.5 MJ/kg of electricity. The use of combustion of fossil fuels is the dominant contribution to the products GHG emissions. Environmental data are based EPD for suppliers to the domestic Swedish market.
Resources.Name: Bricks
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of. Bricks in buildings usually does not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life. Bricks are suitable for reuse.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Bricks are normally used in Sweden without glaze and different size occurs from different producers and common standard formats is produced as well (228x108x54 mm). Brick can be used for load bearing structures or for decorative and functional purpose when used exterior or interior. Brick is used indoor in interior walls, but is not so common in Sweden. Facing bricks is a modern alternative as facade cladding.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The technology used by the manufacturers is similar, but the fuel varies, with natural gas and oil being predominant. An addition of limestone powder to the clay produces yellow bricks. For brown or brown-black bricks, manganese is used. Roof tiles are fired in cassettes at 1050°C. The firing process itself takes two days in a modern tunnel kiln. The entire process is monitored to ensure that all roof tiles achieve uniform hardness and are frost-resistant.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are representative of the bricks that are consumed on the Swedish market. Environmental data is based on the producers EPD collected during 2020.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative for bricks used on the Swedish market.

Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Lightweight expanded clay concrete blocks used in Sweden are mainly manufactured in Sweden, but import occurs.
Resources.ComparativeProperty:
When expanded clay clinker are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.  As the environmental impact is given per kg, it is important to check the density with what is actually purchased. The guide value of the density for different fractions can be found below:
0-32 mm, 280 kg/m³
2-4 mm 370 kg/m³
2-6 mm, 400 kg/m³
4-10, 300 kg/m³
12-20mm, 260 kg/m³
Resources.GeneralComment: The environmental impact for manufacturing dominates by the clinker production and the amount of cement content in the lightweight aggregate block. Environmental data are based EPD for suppliers to the domestic Swedish market, with a variation from 0.17 to 2.4 kg CO₂e/kg. The figures used here is based on the EPD and recalulations made based on the material mix reported in these EPDs.
Resources.Name: Lightweight expanded clay clinker
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of and usually does not need any maintenance.
Resources.Synonyms: Lightweight expanded clay aggregate (LECA) or expanded clay
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Lightweight expanded clay is used in house constructions for draining as well as in structural backfill against foundations.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The blocks are made from light clinker pellets that is made from low-lime clay, which is shaped into small balls that are then burned in rotating kilns. The clinker pellets are bound with cement, sand and water and are then shaped into blocks. The size and density of the clinker pellets varies, as the binder amount used in the blocks. Some manufacturers use fly ash as complement to cement.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are representative of the sand lime bricks that are consumed on the Swedish market. Environmental data is based on the producers EPD collected during 2020.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative for lightweight expanded clay used on the Swedish market.

Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Stone wool is primarily used as thermal insulation, and is sometimes also used for sound insulation or for a combination of both functions. This type of stone wool product is intended for use in a protected environment.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Stone wool is produced either in an electric furnace or, more commonly, in a cupola furnace. The process also involves the use of additional energy sources which, together with the primary raw materials, contribute to the GWP. The binder content is typically about 5 to 10%. Minor variations in density for the same lambda value exist between different manufacturers, but the density and lambda values provided here are representative of the products used on the market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative of the manufacturing process  and products that is currently consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data is representative of the stone wool product type in the form of batts and rolls, and includes all types of thermal insulation that do not have any surfacing, coatings, or similar treatments. If surfacing is included, a more precise and specific dataset should be selected, as such products typically have a somewhat higher environmental impact per kilogram.

Resources.GeneralComment: GWP (A1-A3) for wood-based panels can vary greatly between different manufacturers. To achieve a comment result, the biogenic carbon stored in products is subtracted, so that the climate impact is reported as GWP-GHG. Even after this, there can be significant differences between manufacturers which, without access to the underlying LCA report, are difficult to explain. One difference may be the environmental impact allocated to the wood raw material. For plywood, climate impact has thus been corrected for a producer (i.e. reduced). The difference after correction is less than 10 % between producers.
Resources.Name: Plywood (spruce or pine)
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part of.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Plywood is commonly used as a surface material in a protected environment from weather exposure or indoors. Plywood is available as unclassified building plywood and as classified structural plywood. Structural plywood is used, for example, behind plasterboards in standard stud walls to allow heavier items to be screwed onto the finished wall. Structural plywood is manufactured in two different classes: 15/50 and 20/70 (bending strength in MPa/modulus of elasticity in MPa).
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Data is valid for plywood made of spruce or pine and about 10 % resin . Densities between different producers varies +/-5 %.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing processes and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data are representative of a plywood consisting of thin wood veneers that are cross-laminated, glued, heat-treated, and pressed under high pressure. This results in a dimensionally stable and strong board.

Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden consists of domestic producers and imports.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: The resource serves as proxy data for various types of rubber products when specific climate data (EPD) is unavailable. Since the density of rubber varies greatly, from 180 to 1400 kg/m³, no specific value is given here. Instead, the density needs to be determined based on the type of rubber for which the GWP data will be applied.
Resources.GeneralComment: Data is for different manufacturers who make different plastic products based on ethylene propylene rubber (EPDM) and neoprene (CR), also called polychloroprene or chloroprene rubber. Environmental data for this resource is based on EPDM and GWP-GHG (A1-A3) is based on a few EPDs and database data.
Resources.Name: Synthetic rubber type EPDM and SBR, unspecified

Names.EN: Synthetic rubber type EPDM and SBR, unspecified
Names.SV: Syntetiskt gummi typ EPDM och SBR, ospecificerat

Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part of.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Synthetic rubber products are used in a lot of applications in building constructions and this resource is used when specific data is missing.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The rubber product is assumed to contain less than 5% additives and fillers.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The resource is a proxy data for all kind of synthetic rubber products whenever specific climate data (EPD) is missing.

Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption of boards in Sweden is based on import.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: This specific board is intended for indoor use, and common thicknesses are 1.7 mm, 3 mm, 4.8 mm, or 6 mm.
Resources.GeneralComment:
Hard board represents a wooden product based on wood fibres manufactured in a wet process. Apart from wood fibres, hard board also comprises no binder (if produced according to the Masonite process) or minor amount binding agents (2%) and additives like wax.
GWP (A1-A3) for wood-based panels can vary greatly between different manufacturers. To achieve a comment result, the biogenic carbon stored in products is subtracted, so that the climate impact is reported as GWP-GHG. Even after this, there can be significant differences between manufacturers which, without access to the underlying LCA report, are difficult to explain. One difference may be the environmental impact allocated to the wood raw material.
Resources.Name: Hard board, HB (wet process)
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Hard board can be used both for building purposes (wall, roof, floor, air gaps) as well as for furniture and furnishings.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The data applies to hard board made of softwood and not oil-hardened, which is about 940 kg/m3 and 1000 kg/m3 respectively. The density may vary between different manufacturers.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Hard board represents a wooden product based on wood fibres manufactured in a wet process.

Resources.Name: Glasswool, batts and rolls
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative for the product type glasswool as batts or rolls and includes all types of thermal insulation that do not include any surfacing. In the case that surfacing is included, a more precise and exact choice should be made; such products typically have higher climate impact per kg.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Glasswool is used as thermal insulation and sometimes also used as sound insulation or as a combined function. Glass wool is intended to be used in a protected environment.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) are valid for non-coated glasswool, batts and rolls. The GWP may vary between 0.7-1.6 kg CO₂e/kg based on the manufacturer. The average data values are based on EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Germany and Poland.
Resources.Synonyms: Glass wool, mineral glass wool, mineral wool, batts, boards, panels, thermal insulation
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Glass wool is produced in an electric furnace. The process involves primary raw materials and energy sources, both of which contribute to the GWP. The proportion of recycled glass used as raw material varies between 40 and 80%. The amount of binder is approximately 5 to 10%. There is a minor variation in density for the same lambda value between different manufacturers, but the density values given here, as well as the lambda value, are representative of the products used on the Swedish market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal to the construction it is part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: To assess thermal insulation, the lambda value must be used in combination with the fact that different product options have different densities. In other words, thermal insulation cannot be compared per kilogram, but rather within a given building application. The material data for the generic resource is as follows: density 18.7 kg/m³ and lambda value 0.035 W/(mK).
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers, but significant import occurs from (given in relative order): Germany, Poland and Europe.

Resources.Name: Glasswool, sound batts
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The product type glasswool, sound batts, includes all types of sound insulation with a density for use sound insulation and do not include any surfacing. In the case that surfacing is included, a more precise and exact choice should be made; such products typically have higher climate impact per kg.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Glass wool is normally used as thermal insulation, but this product type is primarily used for sound insulation. Glass wool is intended for use in a protected environment.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) are valid for sound batts. The GWP may vary between 0.7-1.6 kg CO₂e/kg based on the manufacturer. The average data values are based on EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Germany and Poland.
Resources.Synonyms: Glass wool, mineral glass wool, mineral wool, batts, boards, panels, acoustic, sound, noice reduction
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Glass wool is produced in an electric furnace. The process involves primary raw materials and energy sources, both of which contribute to the GWP. The proportion of recycled glass used as raw material varies between 40 and 80%. The amount of binder is approximately 5 to 10%. There is a minor variation in density for the same lambda value between different manufacturers, but the density values given here, as well as the lambda value, are representative of the products used on the Swedish market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal to the construction it is part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: Assessing noise reduction requires accounting for the product’s air flow resistivity.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers, but significant import occurs from (given in relative order): Germany, Poland and Europe.

Resources.Name: Cement-bonded wood wool
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative for wood wool cement panels. Wood wool panels are made by mixing wood shavings with cement and lime as a binder and any paint.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Wood wool cement panels is used as thermal insulation and also used as sound insulation or a combined function. The panel has an intended use in a protected environment. It is not needed to add fire retardant in a wood wool cement panel.
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP-GHG (A1-A3) applies to panels and can vary between different manufacturers and is based on some EPDs from several suppliers. The environmental impact of wood is low, but the contribution from the binder has a significant effect on why the type of binder and the proportion affect the result GWP-GHG (A1-A3), as well as the proportion of biogenic carbon that the product contains.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The product typically contains around 33% wood wool, 50% cement, 10% lime and water. There is a variation in the density between 400-500 kg/m³ for the same lambda value. The density given here and the lambda value are exemplary values of what is used in the market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: In order to assess thermal insulation, the lambda value needs to be used in combination with the fact that different product alternatives have different densities. With other words, thermal insulation cannot be compared per kg but in use conditions. Material data applicable for the generic resource is 450 kg/m³ and lambda λ 0.085 W/(mK).
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is mostly based on import.

Resources.Name: Bitumen waterproofing membrane, bottom layer
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Polymer bitumen-based waterproofing layers are bitumen mats with reinforcement and cover mass of polymer bitumen on both sides. A distinction is made between two types of polymer bitumen: elastomer bitumen (PYE) and plastomer bitumen (PYP). Data are representative for a PYE top layer bitumen waterproofing membrane used on the Swedish market. In the Nordic countries is bitumen waterproofing almost exclusively uses bitumen modified with SBS (styrene-butadiene-styrene).
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Bitumen-based waterproofing layers are mainly used on roofs and are normally laid in several layers, but there are also alternatives with one layer, but then requires a roof with a roof slope of at least 1:2 - 1:20.
Resources.GeneralComment: The generic values are based on the market situation in Finland that is assumed to be representative for all Nordic countries and information gathered from the largest manufacturers products for bitumen roofing. The data for GWP A1-A3 are based on data gathered from said manufacturers and represent the common products. These manufacturers represent over 95 % of the Finnish bitumen roofing market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The manufacturing is done by heating the raw materials (bitumen and copolymers) to a specific temperature and mixing them. After this the mix is applied to the reinforcing structure (polyester or glass fibre). The resulting sheet is cooled and then faced with mineral granules. The bitumen is generally delivered as hot from the petroleum refinery to the manufacturing site, where it’s heated further. Significant differences arise mainly from the amounts of bitumen and the SBS used in the products. As SBS has a large share of emission, using alternative copolymers to modify the bitumen would also change the GWP-GHG A1-A3 value.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of the manufacturers of bitumen waterproofing layers and the products consumed on the Swedish market. The data on environmental impact are based on LCA calculations and have been compared with cross-sectoral EPDs for all European producers, where these values ​​for GWP are slightly higher.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: For modern bitumen-based waterproofing systems, a service life of up to 40 years can be assumed today.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When bitumen-based waterproofing systems are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is dominated by domestic production, but some imports do occur.

Resources.Name: Window, wood/aluminium, side hung, triple-glazed
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data are representative of a painted wooden window with aluminium cladding and a triple-glazed insulating glass unit.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Windows are made fixed or openable. Balcony and terrace doors are also included in this product group.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for a wood/aluminium window varies between 1.8-2.5 kg CO₂e/kg dependent on type of window. The data values are based on the EPDs from Sweden.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The difference in the manufacturing process and the composition of the windows is small between the Swedish manufacturers. Specific data have been used for window manufacturing and mainly generic LCA data for various inputs.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of the type of window used on the Swedish market. The information is valid until new data are published.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life depends on the maintenance of the product but is normally equal to the service life until a future significant rebuild, which here is set at 50 years.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When comparing different window products, it is important to consider differences in U-value. In addition, the surface weight should be taken into account; for the reference window, this is 39.2 kg/m².
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is dominated by domestic producers, but minor import occurs.

Resources.Name: Particle board
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative for a standard construction chipboard without special treatment or additive materials. If such a variant of the board is used, an EPD can be used if possible or this data can be used as a proxy.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Standard particle board is typically used as surface material in a protected environment, typically indoors.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for standard chip board typically varies between 0.35-0.45 kg CO₂e/kg based on Nordic and Middle-European EPDs. The average data values are based on EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Norway and Finland.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Chipboards are made of wood chips and resin pressed together. The amount of glue is about 10 %. By-products from the manufaturing of sawn timber are utilised in the production of chipboards. Densities vary between 650 and 750 kg/m³.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process  and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: A particle board can have different treatment, coating, etc. that is applicable to different applications that are not considered here but apply to a standard product.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers, but significant import occurs from (given in relative order): Norway, Finland and Europe.

Resources.Name: Floor screeds < 17 % cement
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data is representative of floor screeds containing a maximum of 17% cement, including aluminate cement, burnt/slaked (hydrated lime), hydraulic/burnt lime, ALAG (aluminous aggregate), and other calcined raw materials, excluding by-products such as blast furnace slag and fly ash, and potentially up to 1% fiber reinforcement. If additional properties for concrete are required, information from a supplier must be used.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Floor screeds are intended for indoor use, for smoothing and as a base for further surface coverings, such as carpet or parquet. The products are supplied by the manufacturer as a pre-mixed dry mortar containing all components except water, which is added at the worksite.
Resources.GeneralComment: Floor screeds are made of aggregates, fillers, polymers, and additives. The data provided, based on the concrete’s strength class, reflect commonly used concrete mixes on the market. Factory data for module A3 are based on information from a large number of EPDs. Of the stated value for climate impact, the contribution from the manufacturing process (A3) is relatively small compared to the cement-based binders, which normally account for more than 80% of the climate impact in modules A1–A3.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The concrete's strength class complies with the standards SS-EN 206:2013+A1:2016 and SS 137003:2015.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The manufacturers mix the various raw materials used for the product. The sand used can potentially be sourced locally and dried. The technical representativeness is therefore defined by the product’s technical performance declaration.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of and do not require maintenance.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When concrete floor screed products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Manufacturers of floor screeds are primarily domestic, but imports, mainly from Germany, also occur.

Resources.Name: Stone wool, roof board
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data is representative of the stone wool product type in the form of batts or rolls, and includes all types of thermal insulation that do not have any surfacing, coatings, or similar treatments. If surfacing is included, a more precise and specific dataset should be selected, as such products typically have a somewhat higher environmental impact per kilogram.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Stone wool is primarily used as thermal insulation, and is sometimes also used for sound insulation or for a combination of both functions. This type of stone wool product is intended for use in a protected environment.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) are valid for non-coated stone wool. The GWP may variy between 0.6-1.6 kg CO₂e/kg. The average data values are based on market share and EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Finland and Norway.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Stone wool is produced either in an electric furnace or, more commonly, in a cupola furnace. The process also involves the use of additional energy sources which, together with the primary raw materials, contribute to the GWP. The binder content is typically about 5 to 10%. Minor variations in density for the same lambda value exist between different manufacturers, but the density and lambda values provided here are representative of the products used on the market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative of the manufacturing process  and products that is currently consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: In order to assess thermal insulation, the lambda value needs to be used in combination with the fact that different product alternatives have different densities. In other words, thermal insulation cannot be compared per kg, but instead in use conditions. Material data applicable for the generic resource are as follows; density 180 kg/m³ and lambda 0.038 W/(mK).
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by Nordic producers and Germany (in the following order): Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Finland and Norway.
